Manufacturers sold them in the 1930s and 1940s; in 1958 one maker advertised one but did not put it into production, and only from 1969 to 1975 did it go into production. From the mid-1960s another maker produced them continuously; in the early 1970s Max Mathews began developing one and completed it in 1984. More brands appeared in the 1980s, and commercial success widened after the 1990s.

The electric violin is a violin fitted with an electronic output, usually meaning a design with a built-in pickup and mostly a solid body, though it can also mean an amplified violin with a pickup added. It belongs to the violin family of chordophones, sounded by bowing and also by plucking; the pickup may be magnetic, piezo or electrodynamic, and the signal is processed through an amplifier or effects. Its Hornbostel–Sachs number is 513. It is common in rock, pop, metal, folk rock, jazz, country, new-age and experimental music, while classical players mostly use it for contemporary classical music.
電小提琴琴身多採實心設計以減輕重量，近年建造材料包括克維拉、玻璃纖維與碳纖維。拾: The body of the electric violin is often solid to keep the weight down, and recent materials include Kevlar, fibreglass and carbon fibre. As for the pickup, the piezo element may be a ceramic disc, cylinder or plastic film; a magnetic pickup needs strings wound with iron-containing metal or with a steel core, and synthetic-core or steel-core strings can also be used in systems that make the string itself the pickup element. 電小提琴的音色取決於拾音方式與琴身：實體琴身避免高音量回授，使聲音較原聲小提琴更: The timbre of the electric violin depends on the pickup and the body: a solid body avoids feedback at high volume and makes the sound rougher and sharper than an acoustic violin, while a semi-hollow design can come close to the acoustic sound. The range depends on the number of strings, and a lower string can extend it downwards. Volume and timbre are controlled by the signal sent to an amplifier or PA, and delay, reverb, chorus, distortion and other effects can be added, unlike the traditional violin, which sounds by hollow-body resonance.
